Question: An automobile travels \(\frac{a}{6}\) feet in \(r\) seconds. If this rate is maintained for \(3\) minutes, how many yards does it travel in the \(3\) minutes?
Solution:
First express the speed per second so that we can use the full travel time. Since \(r>0\) is an elapsed time, the speed is
\[
\frac{a/6}{r}=\frac{a}{6r}
\quad\text{feet per second}.
\]
Three minutes is \(3\cdot60=180\) seconds. Using distance equal to speed times time, the automobile travels
\[
\frac{a}{6r}\cdot180=\frac{30a}{r}
\quad\text{feet}.
\]
There are \(3\) feet in a yard, so divide by \(3\). The distance is \(\boxed{10a/r}\) yards, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
